newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast CARB diesel extends decline Friday.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast CARB diesel extends decline Friday.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot CARB diesel fuel fell under pressure Friday from continued cuts in "rack" prices and lower NYMEX values, traders said.
"Racks," where trucks pick up refined product for distribution, have fallen substantially the last week, driven by ARCO, traders said.
Rack prices fell two cents Friday to around 64 cents.
The ongoing declines have put pressure on the price of diesel at refineries, which ship to "racks" via pipelines.
CARB diesel in Los Angeles was pegged 59.50/60.50 cents a gallon Friday, down 3.50 cents a gallon from Thursday.
"Still ARCO's dropping the racks everyday," one broker said, unable to explain the cuts.
Earlier, ARCO declined comment except to say competition determines rack prices.
Traders have speculated a damaged processor at the company's Los Angeles refinery may have backed-up diesel fuel and forced price cuts.
The energy futures market, which influences spot trade, also dampened values Friday, with unleaded gasoline for June delivery falling 2.11 cents a gallon to 60.52 cents.
June crude oil fell 31 cents a barrel to $19.60.

Traders said price discussions have begun on reformulated gasoline in West Coast wholesale markets, following Arizona's announcement last month it would require cleaner fuels in the Phoenix-area in June.
Traders heard RFG offered at 63.50 cents a gallon on Friday, one cent over conventional grade, which will be sold in the Las Vegas, Nevada, market.
CARB grade, which is sold in California, was talked 64.50/65.50 a barrel Friday, down 2.50 cents.
"It's in sympathy with the (New York Mercantile Exchange)," a trader said.
